proposals.impact: lift open rate on lower-performing automations by testing a subject-line pattern from the 66% performer
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance sits at 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Worship sits at 37.5% across 16 sends and Money Avoidance at 52.63% across 19 sends. That is a 29-point gap between the top and bottom automations. Subject lines are the single-file, pre-open lever. The Vigilance sequence is doing something the Worship sequence is not. Studying the Vigilance subject line and applying its structural logic to the Worship sequence is the lowest-risk, highest-signal move available.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of Money Worship Email 1 to match the tone pattern of whichever Vigilance subject line is driving that 66% open rate. Without direct file access Fred cannot read the live Vigilance subject, so the proposal below replaces the likely generic Worship subject with a specific, curiosity-led line rooted in the ICP's lived experience: the person who earns well, tells themselves money is just a tool, and wonders why they still feel oddly tense when a big invoice lands. The new subject line borrows nothing from hype. It names the quiet contradiction that people who over-value money rarely admit to feeling.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Do you see money as the answer to everything?
proposals.new_text: Subject: You tell yourself money is just a number. So why does a big invoice still make your chest tighten?

proposals.impact: unblock automated blog publishing — queue is near-empty (1 post) and the workflow has failed
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 07:06 on 13 June. The content queue shows 1 post queued and 47 published. At the current cadence Joel needs the automated pipeline running or the queue empties within days and organic SEO traffic has nothing new to find. The workflow failure is logged, the path is blocked from Fred editing directly, but Fred can produce the corrected workflow YAML as a ready-to-paste diff so Joel can apply it in one file edit.
proposals.proposal: The Daily Blog Post workflow is most likely failing on a missing or rotated secret, a changed Node version, or a broken Astro build step introduced by a recent dependency update. The fix below adds an explicit Node version pin (20.x, LTS as of June 2026) and a clean install flag to rule out lockfile drift. Joel should paste this into .github/workflows/daily-blog-post.yml, replacing only the setup-node and install steps. If the failure is actually a secret rotation, the same file edit is the right place to confirm the secret name matches what is stored in GitHub Settings > Secrets.
proposals.current_text:
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 'lts/*'
      - run: npm ci
proposals.new_text:
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'
          cache: 'npm'
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline

proposals.impact: close the open-rate gap between Money Worship (37.5%) and Money Vigilance (66.7%) by rewriting the first email's opening
proposals.observation: The quiz recorded zero sessions and zero starts across a 48-hour window. The three automations are firing (combined 47 sends), which means email subscribers exist and are active. Those subscribers arrived from somewhere, and the quiz is not converting any of that traffic into new starts. Either the quiz is not being linked in the active automations, or the landing page above the quiz fold is not giving people a clear reason to begin. This is a copy problem solvable in one file edit.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the hero paragraph on the quiz landing page. The current text (below) describes what the quiz is in abstract terms. The ICP at 25-35 does not need a description of a quiz. They need to feel that the next four minutes will show them something true about themselves that spreadsheets have never shown. The replacement copy is grounded in the gym-bag-on-the-kitchen-floor specific register Joel's brand requires. It names the contradiction: earning well, reading the right things, still not building. That is the thing they won't look at, and naming it precisely is what earns the click.
proposals.current_text: Find out your money personality type and get a personalised action plan to start building real wealth today.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. You have read the books. You have set the budget at least twice.

Something still is not adding up, and you suspect it is not the spreadsheet.

This four-minute quiz identifies the specific way your thinking about money works against the decisions you already know how to make. Joel built it from his MSc Behavioural Economics research and a decade of client work. The result is a short, grounded profile and a set of honest questions worth sitting with.

No email required to see your result.
